resources.string: Allow Nearby devices (Bluetooth) so the app can reach your AuthKey.
Not paired. Pair AuthKey-ESP32 in Bluetooth settings (the AuthKey shows a 6-digit code: press OK if it matches).

Turn on AuthKey as a passkey provider: Android then offers \"AuthKey security key\" whenever a site or app asks for a passkey. The app talks to the AuthKey over Bluetooth, or over USB when it is plugged into the phone; you approve on the AuthKey\'s screen.
Android only lets apps provide passkeys from Android 14 on; this phone is older. Use the QR routes below instead: on a passkey screen choose \"Use another device\" so it shows a QR code.

QR codes, like the Windows helper: a passkey QR (\"Use a phone or tablet\" / \"Use another device\") makes the AuthKey sign in like a phone, over its WiFi. Scan a QR on another screen with the camera. For a QR on this phone\'s screen, add the \"AuthKey QR\" tile to Quick Settings and tap it, or share a screenshot to AuthKey. Authenticator (otpauth) QRs are added to the AuthKey\'s codes when it is plugged in over USB.
Scan a QR with the camera

Locks the phone when the AuthKey has been out of range for a while. It only locks after seeing the AuthKey nearby, and each lock pauses it until the AuthKey is back, so unlocking with your PIN while the AuthKey is away doesn\'t lock again.
Lock when the AuthKey is away

Turn on one: Normal (Accessibility → AuthKey) locks like the power button, fingerprint still works. Strict (device admin) needs your PIN after each lock. On Android 13+, if Accessibility is greyed out: App info → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings.

Seconds away: how long the AuthKey must be gone (default 15). Signal limit: weaker counts as away (default -85; try -75 to lock sooner). Android 11 and older also need Location turned on for Bluetooth scanning.
Lets AuthKey lock the screen when your AuthKey-ESP32 goes out of range. Nothing else.
Waiting for the AuthKey to be nearby
Turn on Normal or Strict lock in the app
Locks the screen when your AuthKey-ESP32 goes out of range. AuthKey reads nothing on your screen.
Point at a passkey or authenticator QR code
Camera permission is needed to scan.
Passkey QR found, sending to the AuthKey…
Authenticator QR found, sending to the AuthKey…
Looking for a QR on the screen…
No passkey QR found on the screen. If the app hides its screen, scan it from another device or share a screenshot.
ON: Android may stop the lock
OFF: the lock can\'t keep running

The walk-away lock runs as a service with a small permanent notification; Android keeps such services alive, but battery savers can still stop them. Samsung: App info → Battery → Unrestricted, and Settings → Battery → Background usage limits → Never sleeping apps → add AuthKey. Don\'t swipe the notification channel off.
